Declare the columns: widths, decimal alignment and row titles

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_columns.Rd

plan_columns() declares the columns of this table by name: their relative widths, the ones whose numbers line up at the decimal point, the row-heading columns, and the separator several cols keys are joined with. Named by column, the settings follow a column when the table is reordered or a study has more arms, and they are what a workbook's columns sheet holds. It is not rtf_columns(), which addresses the columns of finished pages by their printed names.

Usage

plan_columns(
  .plan,
  widths = NULL,
  decimal = NULL,
  row_title = NULL,
  auto_width = NULL,
  sep = NULL,
  cell_format = NULL,
  column_widths_twips = NULL
)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

widths

The relative column widths, rtftable(col_rel_width = ). Named by column (c(row_label = 5, .values = 2), .values for every value column) a reordered table keeps them; unnamed, they are one a column in order, as col_rel_width itself. A name that is not a column of the table stops with the names the table has. Each width is a positive finite number: 0, a negative, NA, Inf or a string stops at plan_columns(). A later plan_columns(widths = ) replaces the earlier one as a whole: c(AGE = 1200, SEX = 900) followed by c(AGE = 1500) leaves the width of AGE only. Say every width in one call.

decimal

The columns whose numbers line up at the decimal point (.values for every value column), set_decimal_split()'s cols, by name. A value that is not column names (NA, "", a number) stops at plan_columns(); a name that is not a column of the table stops when the plan is applied, as a widths name does (a hidden column's name is allowed and changes nothing).

row_title

The row-heading columns, rtftable(row_title = ), by name as widths are: a row key's name as table_plan(rows = ) gives it, .values for every value column. A position counts the printed columns: a key hidden with plan_hide() or taken out by page_by is left out. Like widths, a later call replaces it as a whole.

auto_width

TRUE sizes each column to its widest content, as_rtftables(auto_width = ).

sep

The separator several cols keys are joined with in the value columns' names, "____" by default ("Placebo____F"). The spanning header is built by splitting on it, so a key value that contains it is refused.

cell_format, column_widths_twips

as_rtftables()'s cell_format (a formatter, or a list of them one a column) and rtftable()'s column_widths_twips (absolute widths), as they are. A plan gives column_widths_twips or widths, not both.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb; plan_style() for the table's width.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_sort(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

st <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 3),
  variable  = rep(c("AGE", "WEIGHT", "SEX"), 2),
  .label    = rep(c(NA, NA, "F"), 2),
  .kind     = rep(c("continuous", "continuous", "categorical"), 2),
  stat_name = rep(c("mean", "mean", "n"), 2),
  stat      = c(61.2, 72.43, 12, 63.5, 101.8, 9))
demog <- function(st) {
  table_plan(st, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
    plan_cells(continuous = c(Mean = "{mean:.1f}"), categorical = "{n}") |>
    plan_labels(AGE = "Age (years)", WEIGHT = "Weight (kg)", SEX = "Sex") |>
    plan_stub(name = "Characteristic")
}

# Minimal: the heading column three parts wide, each arm two
pages <- demog(st) |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(Characteristic = 3, .values = 2)) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]$col_rel_width
#> [1] 3 2 2

# The arms' numbers lined up at the decimal point too.  A third arm
# needs no change: the names reach it
st3 <- rbind(st, data.frame(
  ARM = "High dose", variable = c("AGE", "WEIGHT", "SEX"),
  .label = c(NA, NA, "F"),
  .kind = c("continuous", "continuous", "categorical"),
  stat_name = c("mean", "mean", "n"), stat = c(62.0, 88.6, 10)))
pages <- demog(st3) |>
  plan_columns(widths = c(Characteristic = 3, .values = 2),
               decimal = ".values") |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]$col_rel_width
#> [1] 3 2 2 2
pages[[1]]$decimal_split$cols
#> [1] 2 3 4
pages[[1]]
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────
#> Characteristic  Placebo  Active  High dose
#> ──────────────────────────────────────────
#> Age (years)                               
#>     Mean         61.2     63.5     62.0   
#> Weight (kg)                               
#>     Mean         72.4    101.8     88.6   
#> Sex                                       
#>     F             12       9        10    
#> 
#> <rtftable> 6 rows x 4 columns
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     relative 3:2:2:2
#>
